## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b27a9339b9e1e74167774748498cb8930e131c82`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json, skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md, skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-query/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md, skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md + packages/client/src/index.ts, packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.test.ts (the two other carriers of the route-owner comment, card #37695 N1)
Security-touching: yes

Inputs read: cards #33773, #34328, #38177, #33875, #37695 (bodies and every comment, dev report 7235492158 included), the PR body, the file list, the net diff against merge base `7605e0c9`, and the check-runs on the head. Remainder at `TIER_DEFAULT` for the lane seat: `.changeset/33773-skills-follow-merged-code-a.md`.

### ① Derived judgments

- No accept-set change and no public-surface change: the diff is skill prose, one eval `expected_output` string, and comments in three `.ts` files. No schema, export, route or runtime line moves. Right.
- Eval case 16: `expected_output` only; `must_contain` (`seal`, `valueFields`, `tenant_id`, `salted commitments`, `expired`) and `must_not_contain` are unchanged and every `must_contain` term is still in the new text. Right.
- Token ceilings: no ceiling row moved; the ratchet gate is in the green lint check-runs. Right.
- Check-runs on the head at read time: 71 runs, 0 failed; all lint, type-check, changeset, spec-liveness, queue-guard and PR-body guards `success`. Four test shards were still `in_progress` (Test Core 1/10 and 5/10, Test UI 12/16 and 15/16); this record does not vouch for them, and the diff reaches tests only through two comments in `i18n-resolver.test.ts`.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch` is right for wording that follows merged behaviour. The comment-only edits in `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/client` publish no behaviour; `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
Clause-②: no — nothing a consumer can author or call is narrowed, widened or re-shaped; body and changeset agree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report `open_questions`: empty. `security_findings`: none.
- Dev flag (out_of_scope_findings): the `filters.md` operator table lost its Category and SQL-equivalent columns. Answered in ④: acceptable, with nit N1.
- Seat question, the two #37695 items "marked out of frame": both are a checkbox on the card itself ("say both, if the budget can pay for them") and both are true on `main`. `packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts` denies an anonymous caller ahead of the provider probe (`shouldDenyAnonymous`), for every route of the domain, and the locales answer spreads `fallbackChain` only when `getFallbackLocale()` answers a non-empty string. "for signed-in callers" and "the declared `fallbackChain`, if any" say exactly that. They belong here.
- SQL push-down: no code path changes; nothing to judge. The query skill now teaches the pushed-down subquery form as the default and the id read as the exception, which is the SQL-first direction.
- Security: the changed hunks teach authentication (the i18n routes answer signed-in callers only), permission behaviour (a relation condition is read as the caller at every hop; an unreadable related record excludes the row) and a tamper-evidence guarantee (`os audit verify`). Hence `Security-touching: yes`; the adopting seat adds the `security` label.

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md` (#33773)** — read against `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/sealer.ts`, `verifier.ts`, `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx` § Sealed audit objects and `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` § `os audit verify`.

- Parts of at most 10,000 rows per chain per hour: holds (`AUDIT_SEAL_MAX_LEAVES = 10_000`, window one hour, settle ten minutes, one chain for rows about no organization).
- `chainField` optional, default `tenant_id`, text or lookup, the injected `organization_id` as example; fixed once checkpoints exist, a change reads `listed_twice`: holds (docs l.241-271; `verifier.ts` fault kind `listed_twice`).
- The parse-refusal sentence (chain column the object lacks, or not one text value, `id`, `created_at`, or in `valueFields`): holds against the docs list. Absorbing the old one-line `valueFields: ['created_at']` block loses nothing.
- Folded examples, shortened separators, the dropped "regulated tenant" clause and "invoices": lossless for an author.

S1 (should-fix) — the opening sentence now says `os audit verify` "exits 1 on a row edited, inserted or deleted outside the platform". For an inserted row that is not what the code does. A row put into an already-sealed hour reads `late` and unsealed (exit 1) only until the sealer's next pass: `sealLate` re-counts every sealed window of the last seven days (`AUDIT_SEAL_LATE_HORIZON_MS`) and seals each unlisted row into a `late` checkpoint, whoever wrote it. From then on `verifier.ts` judges it `late` with `sealed: true`, and `ok` is `faults.length === 0` with no `modified`, `missing` or unsealed row, so the run exits 0 (`cli.mdx`: exit 0 covers "`late` (sealed)"). The insert still shows, as a `late` row in the report, which is what `objects.mdx` claims ("shows when the ledger is verified"). An agent reading the skill would gate CI on the exit code alone and tell its user a forged insert fails the check; after the next hourly pass it does not. The eval case in this same PR already has the accurate wording ("exits 1 on a changed, missing or unsealed row or a chain fault"). Fix: say the same in `lifecycle.md`, and that an insert into a sealed hour is reported as `late`. The previous text ("breaks its signed checkpoints") was loose too, but it named no exit code.

**`skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json` case 16 (#33773)** — against the card's prompt: holds. One checkpoint or consecutive checkpoints of at most 10,000 rows per organization chain; the `chainField` refusal; the verify sentence is accurate to the exit-code table.

- N2 (nit) — the card's done-when names `listed_twice` for both files; the eval says "a chain fault" without the literal. Accurate, less specific.

**`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md` (#34328)** — against `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx` § The Date Key of a Compare Widget and `packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-declared-members.ts`: holds. Window sent as a time dimension named after `dateRange.field` (default `created_at`); undeclared, `400 INVALID_FIELD` naming the remedy; a related-record date path is covered by one date dimension over it under any name; no author-time rule yet (the docs page says the same). Moving the `dimension` example into the table row and dropping the two-line fragment loses nothing.

**`skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` (#38177, #37695 N2/N3 and the two registration facts)** — against `packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts` (l.985-1004, l.3028-3058), `packages/spec/src/contracts/i18n-service.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` (l.4007-4052) and `packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts`: holds. The stale docstring aside is gone and the double-brace advice stays; `os serve` auto-registers only when no i18n plugin is present, so "You do not need to wire" is the true form; `getSourceLocale()` answers the declared value only, else `undefined`; the two registration facts are judged in ③.

- N3 (nit) — "An activity-milestone summary (`_milestones.{field}.{value}`) keeps its authored `{field}` tokens": the first `{field}` is this file's path-placeholder notation, the second is the literal token an author writes. The same spelling in one sentence carries two meanings, and the path stops short of `.summary`.

**`skills/objectstack-query/SKILL.md` and `rules/filters.md` (#33875, with the #34565 note 6937743380)** — against `packages/objectql/src/relation-filter-lowering.ts` (`RELATION_FILTER_ID_CAP = 1000`, `RELATION_CONDITION_MAX_HOPS = 3`, refusals `dotted-key` and `hop-limit`), the `readableIdsLeaf` declarations (`driver-sql`, `driver-memory`; absent on MongoDB and OData) and `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx` l.686-760: holds, sentence by sentence. One subquery per relationship on the four read verbs with no id list and no cap; refusal before any read on a driver without the bit; three relationships, a fourth and a dotted key refused `INVALID_FILTER` / 400; the cap only where ids are read (multi-valued, `update` / `delete`, and the four read-verb fallbacks the docs list); the caller's scope at every hop, `$ne` included. "one level" and "up to 1000 related ids" are gone from both files and from the Which Tool table.

- The lossy cut (seat note): `filters.md` § Operator Reference is now one example per operator. A reader reaches a rules file from `SKILL.md`, whose **Filter Operators** section carries purpose and SQL for all 19, and `filters.md` names that section. The reader still gets what it needs. Accepted.
- N1 (nit) — two pointers went stale with the cut. `filters.md` still says `$like` / `$ilike` reach is "narrower than the rest of the table", and there is no table now. `SKILL.md` § String Operators still says "Full table, `$like` portability and the `$ilike` boundary: filter rules", while the fuller table is now `SKILL.md`'s own; the two files point at each other for it.

**`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`, `i18n-resolver.test.ts`, `packages/client/src/index.ts` (#37695 N1)** — against `packages/services/service-i18n/src/i18n-service-plugin.ts` ("`registerRoutes` and `basePath` are gone", #23347) and `i18n-route-ledger.ts` ("it mounts none"): the dispatcher is the one mounter, either provider can sit behind `GET /i18n/locales`. All five comments agree with the tree.

- N4 (nit) — the `ResolvedFieldLabel` docblock now says both serving surfaces "once derived this map", and three lines on still says "the 'dedicated method' branch both surfaces check first is dead" in the present tense; one of the two surfaces no longer exists.

Open on this head: S1. Nits N1 to N3 are on prose faces and may ride the S1 fix; N4 sits in a spec comment and may be left as an accepted deviation.
